;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[Israel]] launches an investigation into a video appearing to show soldiers cheering as a [[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] man is shot by an [[Israel Defence Forces|Israeli sniper]] through the [[Israel–Gaza border|Gaza]]n border fence. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/israel-strikes-gaza-after-explosive-devices-found-on-border/2018/04/09/2dfac7ae-3bb9-11e8-955b-7d2e19b79966_story.html?noredirect=on (''The Washington Post'')]
**The [[Palestinian Authority]] pays salaries to its [[West Bank]] staff but not to staff in the [[Hamas]]-controlled [[Gaza Strip]], amid growing disputes between the two groups. [http://www.thesundaily.my/news/2018/04/10/pa-employees-gaza-go-unpaid (''The Sun Daily'')]
*[[Terrorism in Thailand]]
**Three bombs explode in [[Sungai Kolok]], [[Narathiwat]], [[Thailand]], injuring four people. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/news/general/1443578/multiple-bomb-explosions-in-sungai-kolok-injure-at-least-4 (''The Bangkok Post'')]
*A motorcycle bomb kills at least eight and injures at least seven at a market in [[Shindand]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/explosion-in-western-afghanistan-kills-8/4338850.html (Voice of America)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[2018 Douma chemical attack]]
***[[Human Rights Watch]] calls the attack a [[war crime]] and says both [[Russia]] and [[Syria]] may bear criminal responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-warcrimes/syria-chemical-attack-is-war-crime-human-rights-watch-chief-idUSKBN1HG28U (Reuters)]
**An explosion in [[Idlib]] kills more than a dozen, including civilians and children. [http://www.euronews.com/2018/04/10/idlib-blast-death-toll-rises-to-at-least-19 (euronews)]
*A prosecutor asks the [[International Criminal Court]] to decide if it has jurisdiction over [[Rohingya]] deportations from [[Myanmar]] to [[Bangladesh]], saying they may constitute a [[crime against humanity]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-icct-rohingya/war-crimes-prosecutor-seeks-jurisdiction-over-rohingya-deportations-idUSKBN1HG30J?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Metropolitan Police]] in [[London]] launches a war crimes investigation into five men wanted in [[Rwanda]] for alleged massacres in 1994. A [[England and Wales|United Kingdom]] court previously refused to extradite the men over concerns they may not receive a [[right to a fair trial|fair trial]]. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/london/london-doctor-accused-of-war-crimes-happy-to-go-to-court-in-uk-a3809161.html (''The London Evening Standard'')]
*Three [[US Navy SEALs]] go [[court martial|on trial]] in [[San Diego]] accused of [[war crimes]]. Prosecutors allege the trio tortured unidentified detainees in Village Stability Platform Kalach in [[Chora District|Chora]], [[Uruzgan]], [[Afghanistan]]. [http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/military/sd-me-seal-trials-20180409-story.html (''The San Diego Union Tribune'')]

;Arts and culture
*"[[Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour]]"
**In a new [[apostolic exhortation]], ''Gaudete et Exsultate'', [[Pope Francis]] mentions [[Satan]] or the [[Devil]] twelve times. Warning against [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] media transgressing the eighth commandment, he calls to "see how the unguarded tongue, set on fire by [[hell]], sets all things ablaze." [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pope-document-holiness-devil/after-no-hell-report-pope-gives-the-devil-his-due-idUSKBN1HG2GY (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*The [[New Zealand]] [[Overseas Investment Office]] approves the sale of [[clothing]] company [[Icebreaker (clothing)|Icebreaker]] to U.S. retail conglomerate [[VF Corporation]], revealing the sale price as [[NZ$]]288 million. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/industries/102837654/exicebreaker-owners-sold-business-for-288-million (Stuff)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2018]]
**A fire breaks out on [[South Korea]]n [[fishing vessel]] FV ''Dong Won 701'' in the [[Timaru|Port of Timaru]], [[New Zealand]]. Ten fire crews and a tug are in attendance. At least three are hospitalised and the ship is evacuated. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/102962522/ship-on-fire-timaru-port (Stuff)] [https://www.radionz.co.nz/news/national/354601/three-suffer-smoke-inhalation-after-ship-catches-fire (Radio New Zealand)]
*A school bus plunges into a gorge in the foothills of the [[Himalayas]], in [[Himachal Pradesh]], [[India]], killing three adults and at least 27 children. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/new-delhi-children-killed-after-school-bus-plunges-into-gorge-india/ (CBS News)] 
*A wall collapses onto playing children in [[Doornfontein]], [[South Africa]], killing three. [https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2018-04-09-deadly-wall-collapse-it-sounded-like-a-big-car-crash/ (Times Live)]
*A school charter bus traveling illegally on a [[parkway]] on [[Long Island]], [[New York State|New York]], collides with a bridge. Dozens of students are injured. [http://abcnews.go.com/US/bus-strikes-long-island-overpass-injuring-high-school/story?id=54329727 (ABC News)]
*The [[Norfolk Southern Railway]] sues two staff members involved in a train collision last month in [[Georgetown, Kentucky|Georgetown]], [[Kentucky]], that derailed 13 cars and injured four. [https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/2018/04/09/lawsuit-2-nky-men-were-negligent-georgetown-train-collision-didnt-stop-time/498631002/ (Cincinnati)]
*A double decker tourist bus collides with low-lying tree branches in [[Żurrieq]], [[Malta]], killing two adults with six others being critically injured. [https://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20180409/local/several-hurt-as-tourist-bus-knocks-low-lying-tree-branches.675887?utm_source=tom&utm_campaign=top5&utm_medium=widget (''The Times of Malta'')]
*A [[Piper PA-24 Comanche]] crashes after takeoff in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]], killing all six people aboard. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation-now/2018/04/09/airplane-crash-tpc-scottsdale-champions-course-golf/501868002/ ''(USA Today)'']
*Investigators say [[Trump Tower]], where a man died in a fire yesterday, had no working smoke alarms. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/09/us/trump-tower-fire/index.html (CNN)]
*A [[Gol Transportes Aereos]] [[Boeing 737]]-800 passenger jet takes off over the top of an [[Brazilian Air Force|Air Force]] [[Embraer C-95 Bandeirante]] that was blocking the runway at [[Brasilia International Airport]]. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4b7412aa&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]

;Health and environment
*The [[International Maritime Organisation]] commences meetings in [[London]] aimed at reducing emissions in the shipping industry, which are presently unregulated. The 1997 [[Kyoto Protocol]] made the IMO responsible for controlling ship emissions. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-43696900 (BBC)]
*[[Prince Albert II]] of [[Monaco]] arrives in [[Edinburgh]] to launch an international conference of oceanographers and environmental experts to discuss the global [[marine environment]], including [[oceanic acidification]] and [[marine debris|plastic pollution]], as well as the local creation of [[Marine Protected Area|Marine Protected Areas]] in [[Scotland]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-edinburgh-east-fife-43703424 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] says [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong-un]] has indicated willingness to discuss denuclearisation. [https://www.voanews.com/a/us-confirms-north-korea-willing-to-talk-about-denuclearization/4338713.html (Voice of America)]
*[[Somalia]] seizes [[US$]]9.6 million from three bags arriving on a [[Royal Jet]] flight from [[Abu Dhabi]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]] in the midst of diplomatic tensions between the nations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/somalia-seizes-96m-uae-plane-mogadishu-180409050734664.html (al-Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[Bill Cosby sexual assault allegations]]
**[[United States|U.S.]] entertainer [[Bill Cosby]]'s sexual assault [[Bill Cosby sexual assault allegations#Criminal proceedings and trial #2|retrial]] begins. As he enters the court a topless woman with the words Women's Lives Matter written on her body charges him and is arrested. [http://www.fredericksburg.com/news/news-wire/topless-protester-charges-at-bill-cosby-as-retrial-begins/article_3971bc7d-70e9-54cf-95f4-9191950c1b54.html (AP via ''Fredericksburg'')]
*[[Terrorism in Finland]]
**Abderrahman Bouanane goes on trial in a courtroom set up within a prison in [[Turku]], [[Finland]], accused of two murders and eight attempted murders in an alleged terror attack. The charges, the first terrorism crimes ever charged in Finland, relate to a stabbing in Turku's main market square. Bouanane is charged  with two counts of terror-related murder and eight counts of attempted murder with a terror-related motive. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/moroccan-knife-attacker-trial-starts-finland-54332278 (ABC)]
*[[Terrorism in the United States]], [[Orlando nightclub shooting]]
**Sixteen survivors use anti-terror legislation to sue [[Google]], [[Twitter]] and [[Facebook]], alleging the firms "provided support and resources" to [[ISIL|the Islamic State]]. [https://www.wsbtv.com/news/trending-now/pulse-survivors-sue-twitter-google-facebook-claim-companies-support-isis/727563534 (WSB-TV)]
*[[Terrorism in France]]
**[[France|French]] police arrest three men and three women accused of involvement in the [[2016 Magnanville stabbing]] by an [[ISIL]] supporter. Local media reports the detainees include police major Maryline Bereaud and her daughter. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/09/france-police-officer-questioned-2016-terrorist-murder-jean-baptiste-salvaing (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Terrorism in Indonesia]]
**[[Islamic extremism|Extremist Muslim]] preacher Kiki Muhammad Iqbal is sentenced to nine years for inciting terrorism for a sermon he gave last year at a mosque in [[Bandung]]. The sermon is alleged to have caused two suicide bombers to launch a May 2017 attack that killed three policemen in [[East Jakarta]]. [http://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/indonesian-preacher-gets-nine-years-jail-for-inciting-suicide-bomb-attack-in-jakarta (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Stormy Daniels–Donald Trump scandal]]
**The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] raid the office, hotel room and home of [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s lawyer and spokesperson [[Michael Cohen (lawyer)|Michael Cohen]], seizing records related to several topics including payments to pornographic-film actress [[Stormy Daniels]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/09/us/politics/fbi-raids-office-of-trumps-longtime-lawyer-michael-cohen.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Around 2,500 police armed with [[tear gas]] launch a raid in [[Notre-Dame-des-Landes]], [[France]], in a bid to force the removal of 250 activists who have occupied the site of the proposed [[Aéroport du Grand Ouest]] for ten years to prevent its construction. The proposed airport is abandoned but the activists refuse to leave their community. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/09/france-notre-dame-des-landes-police-anti-airport-activists-teargas (''The Guardian'')]
*A day after a woman and her family tried to burn themselves in protest alleging she was raped by a local official and her husband murdered whilst in custody, six policemen are arrested in [[Unnao]], [[India]]. [https://www.thequint.com/news/politics/woman-alleges-rape-by-bjp-mla-kuldeep-singh-sengar (The Quint)]
*[[Berlin Half Marathon]], [[terrorism in Germany]]
**Police in [[Germany]] release six men suspected of plotting a terror attack at yesterday's [[Berlin Half Marathon]], one of whom was linked to [[Anis Amri]], after failing to find evidence to substantiate their suspicions. [https://www.thelocal.de/20180409/police-release-six-men-after-no-evidence-found-of-plot-against-berlin-half-maratho (''The Local'')]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[British Transport Police]] reject claims by entertainer [[Olly Murs]] of a cover-up of a possible terror incident in [[London]] in November. Murs reported hearing gunfire but investigations found no evidence of weapons use. [https://news.sky.com/story/british-transport-police-rubbishes-olly-murs-claim-of-terror-alert-cover-up-11324145 (Sky)]
**Six alleged members of banned [[neo-Nazi]] group [[National Action (UK)|National Action]] appear before the [[Central Criminal Court (England and Wales)|Central Criminal Court]]. Two, including the group's alleged leader, are charged with plotting the terrorist murder of MP [[Rosie Cooper]]. [http://www.warringtonguardian.co.uk/news/16148218.Alleged_leader_of_National_Action_appears_in_crown_court/ (''The Warrington Guardian'')] [http://www.sthelensstar.co.uk/news/16147313.Man_accused_of_being_member_of_banned_group_National_Action_in_court/ (''The St. Helens Star'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**The Speaker of the [[Parliament of Catalonia]], [[Roger Torrent]], announces the investiture session of [[Jordi Sànchez i Picanyol]] for Friday, April 13. Sànchez, who has been imprisoned since October 2017 accused of sedition, was nominated again for [[President of the Generalitat of Catalonia|President de la Generalitat]] on April 7. [https://www.larazon.es/espana/torrent-convoca-para-el-viernes-dia-13-el-pleno-de-investidura-de-jordi-sanchez-LP18069828 (''La Razón'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Symphony of the Seas|MV ''Symphony of the Seas'']], the world's largest [[cruise ship]] at 206,912 tonnes, begins its first voyage with paying passengers. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/travel/cruising/102772802/symphony-of-the-seas-worlds-largest-cruise-ship-kicks-off-maiden-voyage (Stuff)]

;Sports
*[[2018 Green Bay Packers season]]
**[[Green Bay Packers]] wide receiver [[Trevor Davis]] is arrested after making a bomb joke at [[Los Angeles International Airport]]. [http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2769170-packers-wr-trevor-davis-arrested-for-making-bomb-joke-at-lax-airport (Bleacher Report)]
